rounds.text: The recent performance of DCG Cables & Wires Ltd reveals a concerning trend in profitability, as the quarterly operating margin has contracted by 5 percentage points compared to the year-ago quarter [E19]. While the company has demonstrated historical sales growth [E8] and margin expansion over a three-year period [E18], the most recent data indicates that this momentum is stalling [E19]. Investors are currently receiving no return on their capital through dividends [E4], which increases the risk profile for a company whose stock is languishing near the bottom of its 52-week range [E5]. Furthermore, the return on equity of 10.4% and ROCE of 13.4% suggest only modest efficiency in generating returns from the capital employed [E6, E7]. Conceded: [E1, E2, E8, E18]. The combination of declining quarterly margins and a lack of dividend yield suggests that the current valuation may be under pressure as the market reacts to these deteriorating operational signals [E4, E19].

evidence.fact: Price-to-book is 1.09x (price ₹ 52.6 on a book value of ₹ 48.4).
The stock sits 18% of the way up its 52-week range (47 low to 79 high).
Compounded sales growth over 5 years is 62%.
Operating margin is 15% in Mar 2026 against 7% three years earlier (+8 percentage points).
Quarterly operating margin is 12% in Mar 2026 against 17% in the year-ago quarter (-5 percentage points).
